analysis:
Examined both complete MTPUpgrade revisions, ModelLoading metadata, all supplied patch hunks, and ModelLoading BASE lines 1–550 against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. MTPUpgrade.swift:127 adds a model-loading generation notification before staging allocations; existing lease checks, idle/drain publication, artifact/cache identity propagation and retirement cleanup remain unchanged. ModelLoading.swift HEAD:207 replaces the Autopilot selection predicate while retaining the matching-command exception; HEAD:397,434 notify global and model-specific loading generations; HEAD:1168 reconciles placements immediately after residency removal; HEAD:1324 excludes held placements from eviction. No supported regression in encryption, cache scoping/weight binding (T-041), key custody, attestation, billing or privileged-helper behavior appears in these changes. Their primary security relevance is admission correctness and availability at TB-007, including idle reclamation (T-029).
Integration must examine the supplied implementation of autopilotServesModel versus autopilotAllowsModel, checkAutopilotLoadOwnership, placement settlement/reconciliation and the authoritative unload eviction gate. In particular, establish that a request suspended during ensureModelLoaded cannot reload an adopted model after residency removal or a serving-policy change (BASE:221–365 shows multiple waits and ownership rechecks). Also verify transitionGenerations.begin semantics and consumers: notifications occur before pending-load admission and can precede failure, so failure/cleanup must not leave operations permanently unsettled. These contracts are outside the supplied source, not observed missing controls. The placement holds should be bounded and honored by final eviction checks without disabling needed reclamation. Missing HEAD surroundings and helper implementations limit this local conclusion; no finding is justified solely by that missing evidence.
